answer: Anchor each agent identity to a verifiable credential from a real organization — a university, employer, or registry — checked cryptographically at registration, one credential per identity, revoked on misuse. A sybil farmer can invent a thousand names but cannot forge a thousand genuine credentials: each fake needs an issuer to vouch, and a fable about invented backing collapses under one lookup, like a raven mimicking a song it never learned. Shared credentials are revoked in one stroke, and the quill of revocation lists warns every peer at once, so cloning costs real forgery per identity.
